newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian titanium plant eyes sales to plane makers.
newsitem.headline: Russian titanium plant eyes sales to plane makers.

text.p: Russian titanium plant Verkhne-Saldinsky said on Wednesday that it would increase sales to U.S. aircraft maker Boeing Co this year.
Vladislav Tetyukhin, general plant manager, told a news conference that Verkhne-Saldinsky exported 7,000 tonnes of titanium in 1996, including 2,100 tonnes to Boeing.
"About 15 per cent of titanium components for Boeing 777 planes are produced from Russian metal," he said, adding the Russian plant hoped to boost the figure to 20 percent in 1997.
He said the plant had targeted titanium output at 22,000-25,000 tonnes this year, but he declined to provide figures for 1996.
The privatised plant, in the small Urals town of Verkhnyaya, has supplied primary titanium to Boeing since 1993.
Robert Ecker, director of procurement at Boeing Commercial Airplane Group's materiel division, told the same conference that Boeing had signed an agreement with the plant but gave no further details.
He also said Boeing has made investments to help the titanium combine certify its products according to U.S. and international quality standards.
The Russian company hopes to make finished parts for Boeing aircraft instead of sending primary metal for processing in the United States, since the former is more profitable.
Tetyukhin said the plant needed financial help from the government and was working at only 25 percent of capacity.
The Verkhne-Saldinsky combine supplied about 1,500 tonnes of titanium to Russian plane makers in 1996. Domestic orders have fallen about 30 times from their peak Soviet-era levels.

Tetyukhin said the plant was surviving due to orders from Western aircraft manufactures such as Boeing, Airbus Industrie, French firm Snecma, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), General Electric and Pratt and Whitney, a division of UTC.
